newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Allied stresses remains on course.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Allied stresses remains on course.

text.p: British drinks to pub group Allied Domecq is on course to meet its full year target with a stronger second half to the year in store, chairman Sir Christopher Hogg said in a telephone interview on Tuesday.
The group's first half profits were in line with its expectations and "the group is on track to meet its full year objectives as a whole," said Hogg.

Allied reported pretax profits at actual exchange rates down one percent at 317 million stg, but expects its second half results to benefit from favourable U.S. spirits shipments and higher first half investment in its pub estate.
Hogg declined to comment on what impact the decision by Grand Metropolitan and Guinness on Monday to merge would have on Allied's business and strategy.
"It's too early to comment in a nutshell. You will appreciate there is a need to analyse and think about many aspects of what is proposed," he said.

However, he said the merger may open up some oppurtunities for Allied, "there will have to be rearrangements of distribution, sale of brands, management fall out. Not to mention the dislocation that occurs when two companies are put together."
